This is because the 2D perovskite film in the 2D control sample is one thin layer, and IPA can dissolve both the 2D perovskite and the organic molecules. Therefore, IPA can wash away all the 2D perovskite and also some of the methylammonium halide and formamidine halide inside the 3D perovskite, which then exposes more PbI . In contrast, after the interface reconstruction 2 method, we can simultaneously remove most of the PbI and n=1 2D perovskite. In this method 2 we obtain just the right amount of n=2 2D perovskite on top, as shown in Figure 5.2b. The key difference between the 2D control washed with IPA and the interface reconstruction is the overloading step. The overloading step provides two functions for the interface reconstruction method: First, because of the overloading of the 2D ligand, we make PbI become a limiting 2 reagent and the 2D ligand becomes an excess reagent, which then forces all the PbI to form the 2 2D perovskite with the 2D ligand. Second, because of the overloading, the formed 2D perovskite is very thick, with the n=1 2D perovskite and extra 2D ligand on the top surface and the n=2 2D perovskite on the bottom. The top surface of the 2D perovskite serves as a protection layer for the bottom layer during the washing. After washing, we wash away the top surface and finally keep just the right amount of n=2 2D perovskite remaining. Therefore, after the interface reconstruction, we can simultaneously remove most of the PbI and obtain phase pure n=2 2D perovskite phase, 2 as summarized in Figure 5.2c. In addition to removing PbI and obtaining phase pure n=2 2D perovskite phase, time- 2 resolved photoluminescence (TRPL) and time-resolved microwave conductivity (TRMC) spectroscopy were also conducted to investigate surface passivation effects. As illustrated in the TRPL measurements (Figure 5.3a), the target films show a 47% increase in carrier lifetime from 5.8 µs (control) to 8.5 µs, indicating the 2D reconstruction process can effectively reduce defect- assisted non-radiative recombination. In contrast, with TRMC (Figure 5.3b), a bulk measurement without surface sensitivity, the carrier lifetime of the target increased merely by 5.3% from 15 µs (control) to 15.8 µs. The TRPL coupled with the TRMC results reveal that the 2D reconstruction process mainly influences the surface while the bulk 3D perovskite remains largely untouched.
